title: Request for a Third Electronic Flight Bag Position on the Flight Deck Centre Pedestal

ata.title: Flight Deck Information — Electronic Flight Bag Unit

abstract: Operator asks for a third electronic flight bag position on the centre pedestal for line training and route checks. The order is held pending a certification position on display placement in the primary field of view.

sections.request: We run a large line training operation and on almost every training sector there is a third person on the flight deck who needs the same charts and the same performance application as the two operating pilots. Today the instructor either leans across or carries a tablet on a knee board, and neither is satisfactory when the aircraft is being flown by a new first officer. We would like a properly installed third position on the centre pedestal, powered from the aircraft and running the same application load as the two installed units, so that the instructor sees exactly what the crew sees. We are not asking for a new application, only for a third window onto the one we already have.
sections.background: We raised the same idea informally at the operators conference in 2025 and were told that the power budget was the obstacle. Since then our fleet has moved to the higher rated unit and we understand the power argument has changed. We currently fly about 9000 training sectors a year across the sub-fleet and our training department estimates that fifteen per cent of instructor workload on those sectors is spent working around the absence of a third display.
sections.expected_outcome: A certified third electronic flight bag position on the centre pedestal with aircraft power, the same application load as the installed units, and no change to the two operating positions. Availability as a retrofit within eighteen months would let us fit it during the planned cabin programme.

type_data.business_justification: The operator estimates that a third display would recover about eleven minutes of instructor attention per training sector, which across 9000 sectors a year is judged equivalent to two additional training aircraft days per month. The benefit is real but entirely internal to the operator's training organisation.
type_data.closure_note: Held in June 2026 pending a certification position. A display on the centre pedestal at the requested height falls inside the area from which the authority expects primary flight information to be excluded, and no precedent exists on this type for a third crew display in that location. The design office is unwilling to open the installation until the placement question is answered, because the answer determines whether the request is a bracket and a power feed or a full flight deck change. The operator was offered a certified stowage for a portable device in the interim and the order will be reopened when the placement position is issued.
